title: cercit
kicker: Credit review for salaried car loans
summary: I turned my vehicle-finance experience into a working loan-review demo. It checks documents and lending rules, explains its recommendation and leaves the final decision with a credit officer.
role: I defined the product, credit policy and requirements, then reviewed and tested the build. Claude wrote most of the code.
alt: cercit credit officer dashboard showing a synthetic application book and exception queue
intro: I have worked in vehicle finance since 2014. cercit applies that experience to a loan-review system: what information to collect, which rules to check and what an officer needs before deciding a case.

sections.title: The loan file
paragraphs: A loan application brings together identity documents, income, credit history and vehicle details. When those disagree or something is missing, an officer needs to see the issue before making a decision.
I defined the first product around salaried new-car buyers. That gave the application a specific document list and a lending policy I could write and review.

sections.title: What I put on the review screen
paragraphs: The system reads and checks documents, compares income sources and runs lending rules. The officer sees the recommendation beside the reasons, affordability calculations and any failed checks.
I kept the final decision with the officer. They can approve, decline or refer a case, and must record a reason. Missing income or bureau information also goes for review.

sections.title: How I directed the build
paragraphs: I wrote the requirements and credit policy, set priorities and checked the resulting workflows. Claude handled most implementation, including the website, database and document services.

I also defined how rule changes should happen. A change is drafted, checked for its effect on cases and approved before it becomes active. The system keeps a record of who changed or overrode a decision.

sections.title: Try it with synthetic cases
paragraphs: You can try the customer and staff journeys using synthetic cases. The public repository includes the requirements, architecture and test documentation.
The demo shows the workflow. To measure its effect on approval time or credit quality, the next step would be a lender pilot with agreed measures and representative cases.

title: Ownly Together
kicker: Group food ordering for Ownly's Chennai launch
summary: A group-ordering concept for Rapido's zero-commission food app. One link brings the group in, each person pays only their share, and the bill splits to the paisa. I took it from research plan to a live, tested prototype.
alt: Ownly Together case study: order together, pay your share, no more chasing, with the live prototype's order confirmation and map

title: Wrong UPI payment recovery
kicker: Request recovery from the payment receipt
summary: After a wrong UPI payment, the sender needs a clear way to act. I designed a recovery request on the receipt, a return flow for the recipient and a status tracker for the sender.
role: I defined the problem, prioritised features and wrote the requirements and sprint plan. AI tools helped with research and the prototype.
alt: Prototype payment receipt with an action to request recovery
intro: This is a product concept for someone who has sent money to the wrong UPI ID. I designed what happens after they notice the mistake: how the sender raises and tracks a request, and how the recipient responds.

sections.title: Start with the receipt
paragraphs: I put the recovery action on the payment receipt because it already has the transaction details. Those details carry into a prefilled request, reducing what the sender has to type.
The sender receives a case ID and a timeline showing the status and next step.

sections.title: Give the recipient a way to respond
paragraphs: The recipient can return the full amount, offer a partial return or say that the payment was intentional. I included these paths because a recovery request needs an answer at the other end.
A suspected scam follows a separate fraud route. The recovery flow also checks whether a payment is eligible before raising a request.

sections.title: Turn the screens into planned work
paragraphs: I broke the chosen features into nine user stories and 48 acceptance criteria, with a proposed nine-week delivery plan.

A return payment could expose the sender's phone number through their UPI ID, so the plan uses a masked name. I also added a separate Help entry: an ineligible payment still needs a route to support when the recovery button is hidden.

sections.title: What is public to read and open
paragraphs: The public study contains the requirements, competitor comparison, clickable prototype and sprint plan. Personas and quotes are illustrative; this is an independent concept, with no PhonePe affiliation.
The prototype demonstrates the screens and choices. Bank integration, real-user interviews and a support-team review would be needed before it could process recovery requests.

title: HireMate
kicker: Interview practice for bank and NBFC jobs
summary: I designed a mock-interview concept for freshers and career switchers applying to banking roles. The work includes role-specific questions, a small survey, a clickable prototype and a pricing and launch plan.
role: I chose the audience, designed the research and defined the product and launch plan. AI tools helped develop and check the material.
alt: HireMate prototype for role-specific banking interview practice
intro: HireMate focuses on interviews for collections, field sales, credit and data-analysis roles. I worked on the product strategy and prototype as part of my product-management programme.

sections.title: Make practice specific to the role
paragraphs: I narrowed the audience to Indian freshers and early-career switchers seeking bank and NBFC jobs. The practice covers situations they could face in those roles, including customer handling.
The project has 48 scenarios, with weak answers and suggested corrections. The prototype shows how a candidate chooses a role, practises and receives feedback.

sections.title: What the research told me
paragraphs: The survey collected 14 completed responses. Six came from people in the target roles, so the sample is too small to settle demand or pricing.
I also used 14 AI-simulated persona interviews to develop questions and hypotheses. I kept those separate from the real survey because simulated answers cannot establish what customers want.

sections.title: Check the strategy before using it
paragraphs: I recorded prompts, decisions and corrections in a process log. Source checks caught six errors in AI-generated market research.
The final material includes the audience choice, proposed pricing, first product scope and launch plan. The 10,000-user figure is a launch target.

sections.title: What I would test next
paragraphs: The strategy, landing page and prototype are public. The product is at the concept stage.

The next useful test is with more candidates in the chosen roles: can they use the feedback to give a better second answer, and would they return for another session? That evidence would help decide what to build and charge for.

title: pagefit
kicker: Reduce wasted space in generated PDFs
summary: I worked on a PDF tool that checks the pages after rendering. It adjusts spacing within set limits, then keeps the change only if it reduces wasted space without shrinking the text too far.
role: I defined the layout problem, readability limits and output checks. AI tools helped implement the tool.
intro: Generated PDFs often leave large gaps or push a small section onto another page. pagefit checks the result and tries another layout when there is room to improve it.

sections.title: Look at the finished pages
paragraphs: The tool converts Markdown, Typst or a web page to PDF, then measures how much of each page's text area is used.
Headers and footers are excluded. Including a page number at the bottom would make an almost empty page look full.

sections.title: Stop before the text gets too small
paragraphs: I set limits on type size and margins. The tool tries slightly tighter settings and keeps them only if page count or fill improves.
If it cannot absorb an awkward page within those limits, that page stays.

sections.title: The documented example
paragraphs: The repository records a study document changing from 26 pages to 17, with mean page fill rising from 72% to 96%. That result belongs to that document.
The code and instructions are public. The tool runs locally and reports what the layout loop changed.

sections.title: Checking more document types
paragraphs: Long tables, quotations and illustrated pages need different checks. A useful next test set would compare page count with the actual reading experience, including broken tables and stranded headings.

title: SamsMind
kicker: A public map of notes from my second brain
summary: I built a personal system to capture notes, file them and ask questions of them. A public slice of 47 notes I chose to share is live as a map you can search and read.
role: I defined the note workflow, privacy rules and filing areas, chose which notes to share, then reviewed the implementation built with AI tools.
alt: SamsMind public notes shown as a map of connected dots, coloured by Projects, Areas, Resources and Archives
intro: SamsMind brings capture, filing, search and questions into one workflow on my laptop. The public site shows only the notes I approved for sharing.

sections.title: Use the areas I already have
paragraphs: A saved note receives an ID and timestamp. The filing step chooses from my existing areas (Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives) instead of creating new categories each time.
I can find a note through search or a map of connected notes. Both open the same saved material.

sections.title: Answer with the source attached
paragraphs: The question feature cites the notes used in its answer. A notes-only setting tells it to say when the answer is missing.
If an answer includes general knowledge, that part is labelled separately so I can tell it apart from my saved notes.

sections.title: Decide where the data goes
paragraphs: Personal notes use local processing. If that route is unavailable, they wait rather than being sent to a cloud model.
The public site is a separate export of notes I marked shareable. The private collection and the app itself stay on my laptop.

sections.title: The public map
paragraphs: Each dot is a note and lines join related notes. You can hover to preview, click to read, or search.
It is read-only. Capture, sorting, linking and questions run only in the private app.

title: World of Coins
kicker: Browse my collection by country and issuer
summary: I organised my coin collection into an interactive catalogue. A map and flag grid lead to each country, then its issuers and coins. I also record when a specimen differs from the catalogue type.
role: I curate the collection, define its organisation and correct specimen details. AI tools helped build the site and process images.
alt: World of Coins catalogue with world-map navigation and curated exhibitions
intro: World of Coins is my personal collection catalogue. I wanted the structure to retain who issued each coin, including dynasties and princely states that sit within a modern country.

sections.title: Country is only the first level
paragraphs: The catalogue groups coins by country, issuer and ruling authority. India, for example, includes historical issues as well as the Republic.
The map and flag grid open the same view. Search helps reach countries that are hard to select on the map.

sections.title: Describe the piece I own
paragraphs: A Numista entry describes a coin type. My specimen may be a restrike, replica or have a different composition.
I added specimen notes so those differences are visible. An unknown material stays unknown rather than inheriting a figure that belongs to the original type.

sections.title: Update the collection without rebuilding the layout
paragraphs: The site builds its catalogue from a Numista export. An image-processing step crops coin photographs and removes backgrounds.
Checks compare the country write-ups against the collection records, including material claims and fixed counts.

sections.title: Still cataloguing
paragraphs: The catalogue is a working personal project. I continue adding images and specimen corrections as I catalogue the collection.
The code is public, with source credits for the catalogue data and photographs.

title: WPL data and analytics
kicker: Join cricket performance with squad and auction data
summary: I published a WPL dataset on Kaggle that links match performance, squads and auction records across seasons. A public notebook uses it to ask who was worth the money.
role: I defined the analysis questions and reviewed the dataset structure and the source matching. AI tools helped with processing and with building the notebook.
intro: This project connects WPL scorecards with squad and auction data. The aim is to make questions about spending and performance possible using tables that join consistently. The dataset and the notebook are both public.

sections.title: Connect the records
paragraphs: The dataset has nine CSV files, published on Kaggle under the ODC-By licence. Match IDs connect deliveries and scorecards. Season, team and player identifiers connect those records to squads.
The documented scope covers the 2023–2026 seasons. Anyone can download the files and rebuild the joins.

sections.title: Match names across sources
paragraphs: A player can appear under an abbreviated scorecard name and a full auction name. The dataset uses stable IDs where available and reviewed aliases for the other cases.
The Bangalore-to-Bengaluru team rename is normalised so the franchise stays together in comparisons.

sections.title: Explain the blanks
paragraphs: An unsold player has no sale price. An unpublished fee is also blank, for a different reason. Those cases are documented instead of being filled with an invented average.
The documentation also explains squad members who did not play and describes checks reconciling runs and wickets with the match data.

sections.title: The notebook and its charts
paragraphs: The public notebook, "WPL 2023–2026 records and who was worth the money", has 11 charts.
One question is how squad spend compares with results. The answer still has to allow for the small number of teams and seasons.

facts.label: Programme
facts.value: Masai x iHUB DivyaSampark IIT Roorkee

intro: These are the exercises I did for my product management course. They are practice pieces. They now live on my course site, on the page for each class, so the notes and what I made are in one place.

sections.title: The five published classes
paragraphs: Each class has its own page with my notes and what I made. Class 01, PM with AI, is a PM ecosystem infographic. Class 02, Day in the life, is an infographic on a product manager's day at Cars24.

Class 03, Research methods, is a one-page research plan for Blinkit cart abandonment. Class 04, User interviews, is an AI research prompt tried on Xbox Game Pass. Class 27, GitHub Copilot, is a Snakes and Ladders game with a PRD.

sections.title: Reading the data first
paragraphs: The research session changed how I would start. Secondary research comes before primary research, because existing data tells you who to talk to and what to ask.

It also taught me that what users say and what users do can differ. My Blinkit plan puts secondary data first, then a hypothesis, then a defined group of users. It uses two methods, set up so that a negative result would change the decision.

sections.title: Letting AI draft the questions
paragraphs: For the interview session I ran a structured prompt on Xbox Game Pass. The AI first played back its read of the customer and the journey, and I corrected it. Only then did it draft research questions.

It flagged some of its own questions as leading, such as one that assumed playing through Game Pass is difficult, and rewrote them. The prompt gave me a competent first draft. The judgement was still mine to apply.

sections.title: A small build with a PRD
paragraphs: Snakes and Ladders is a one-file browser game for 2 to 4 players, with an optional computer player. It has 10 snakes and 9 ladders, an exact roll is needed to finish, and a 6 gives another turn.
The game comes with a PRD, and I used GitHub Copilot for the build. The repo lists what I tested, including snake and ladder jumps, the overshoot rule and a full four-player game.
